chose: one shared readJsonOrRefuse seam in floor.ts, throwing the existing Unrunnable, for all three persistent readers (status.json, the ratchet baselines, coherence.config.json)
over: three hand-rolled absent-vs-unreadable checks, one per reader
a new module for the seam
because: three copies of catch-return-default is exactly how green-by-absence got into all three files at once; the repo's redundancy doctrine is derive one spelling from the other. floor.ts already owns this doctrine and already exports Unrunnable, whose CLI renderer is total over every command by construction — so a fourth persistent reader added next month inherits the refusal instead of re-forgetting it.

chose: ownerOf returns string|null — an unowned path has NO owner, and every caller states what it does with that
over: keeping the unconditional "." fallback and filtering the fabricated component out at the scoping seam only
refusing the run when a changed file is unowned
because: the "." fallback is unrepresentable-vs-real confusion at the type: it returns the SAME value for "the root component owns this" and "nothing owns this", so no caller could tell them apart and affectedComponents fed a phantom component into the scope set — verify then announced it had examined component "." that does not exist, graded zero claims, and printed coherent. Refusing would be wrong: an unowned root-level file is ordinary (a config, a script), and the codebase already has the right sentence for it — nothing to check.

chose: correct the floor's partial-collapse premise in all four places it is spelled, and name the mass measures pin as the mitigation — WITHOUT adding a gate
over: gating the node-vanishing collapse (refusing when a component the record remembers is absent from the derived graph)
leaving the comment and fixing only the release notes
because: reproduced the reviewer's shape: 2 remembered claims, one component dropped from the WALK, run printed 'claims: 1 · 1 green · ✓ coherent' exit 0 and laundered the record to 1 in the same run, so a gradual N→1 collapse never meets the floor. The premise 'coverage reds any component whose claims ALL vanished' is only true for a component whose NODE survives with zero claims — coverage iterates the derived graph and cannot see a node the walk dropped. But a gate here would be wrong: deleting a component's spec is legitimate pruning and is observationally identical (this repo evicted two components this release). A documented hole with a named mitigation beats a gate that punishes deletion.

chose: mutation-check the cli.ts generator-guard line itself for the alias bypass
because: no writing command currently declares an alias — resolve, the only one in the registry, writes nothing — so reverting cli.ts to `c.name === cmd` leaves the suite green no matter what oracle is written. Inventing an alias on a generator purely to make a witness would change the public command surface to test it. Answered by moving the flag read behind commandFor(), which IS mutation-checked (collapse it to a name-only match and the registry oracle reds), and by enumerating the generator-refusal oracle from dispatchTokens() so an alias inherits the demand the day one exists.
